correctness.rationale: The sparse n=3 norm reduction is exact: dualize the Perron Rayleigh quotient and two-dimensional Euclidean maximization, then bound F by 9x(1-x)+9(1-x)^2/16<=12/5; the vector (3-i sqrt111,0,3+i sqrt111) realizes input 2 sqrt15 and output 8. For n=2 triangle inequality yields norm one. For n>=4 two disjoint weight edges create a two-dimensional top eigenspace at 1/2; one or two weak coupling edges of magnitude |epsilon|/n give exactly the asserted first-order splittings. Checked symbolic certificate and finite spectral diagnostics in CHECKER.py. Higher-dimensional leading coefficients are for each fixed n. No overall n=3 operator norm is claimed.

originality.rationale: The theorem concerns norm amplification by the complementary arithmetic-mean projection on periodic coefficient vectors. The motivating 2023 full text establishes the coefficient numerical-radius norm, general Banach-limit bounds, and norm-one multiplier/shift operators, not the complementary projection; exact three-period sparse sharpness and the dimension-wide degeneracy-splitting obstruction are additional assertions. published-finding corpus semantic searches with exact objects, aliases and the 4/sqrt(15) constant found no dominating same-claim record. This is a best-knowledge assessment, not a claim of exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: Sharif 2023 motivates studying operator norms relative to numerical-radius norms and identifies norm-one examples, but centering is a natural complementary operator whose contractivity is unresolved by those examples. The theorem fully determines the period threshold for norm nonexpansivity for all n>=2, not one arbitrary example. Its exact sparse amplification in the first exceptional dimension and perturbative eigenvalue-splitting coefficients explain how and why the failure starts; no general unrestricted norm formula is claimed.
